reviewerErrorsAtV1.disclosure: I rejected v1 on one finding. Codex found two more and was right on both. I record them separately because they are different failures.

keyValueMismatch.what: v1's member was keyed leftoverDesignOpenIsAFinding while its value said the opposite — that leftover-design/OPEN is the token, not a finding.
keyValueMismatch.howIMissedIt: I read the value, checked it against DR-105's live OPEN cell, found it correct, and praised it in my verdict as the right inversion from DR-104. I never read the key. A name that contradicts its own value is a heading-versus-body mismatch, which is a defect class I have charged in this corpus before; here I walked past it because the half I checked was right.

fxAuthoringGap.what: The fourteen FX fixture classes are specifications, not implementations, so authoring them is leftover-design. v1 never mentioned them — FX occurs zero times in it.
fxAuthoringGap.howIMissedIt: I enumerated D-042's and D-093's remaining-unmet lists, which is how I found the actor-join gap, and stopped there. I never enumerated the pinned truth tables' own acceptanceEvidenceFixtureClasses container, even though the join pins both v2 and v9.

reviewerErrorsAtV1.pattern: Across the DR-103, DR-104 and DR-105 joins, every finding either of us raised came from enumerating one pinned source's own inventory. I have now missed three such inventories — v11's open decisions, v4's identityDependencies, and v9's fixture classes — and caught one, D-093's unmet list. The corrective is not judgement but coverage: enumerate every inventory a pinned source carries, not the first one that yields a finding.

scopeBoundaryChecked.question: v9 carries fourteen identityDependencies of its own. OBL-PTT-V9 declines to enumerate them, saying the ID-DEP rides stay on that candidate. Is that principled, given that at the DR-104 join I advised carrying an omitted identityDependencies ride?
scopeBoundaryChecked.answer: Yes, and the two cases are consistent rather than in tension. At DR-104 the join had already enumerated four of five v4 rides, so the fifth's absence was an internal inconsistency. Here the join enumerates none of v9's rides and says why: v9 binds NOTHING and is not applied, so building a DR-105 leftover inventory from its dependency ledger would invent leftover the adopted record does not carry. The adopted sources for DR-105 leftover are D-042 and D-093, and those are covered. I checked the one ID-DEP that does overlap them — ID-DEP-P4, execution of every fixture class riding DR-G09 — and it is carried as OBL-G09-EXECUTION.
scopeBoundaryChecked.note: ID-DEP-P13 is recorded in v9 as the one ride in its list with no owner named. That sits inside an unapplied candidate and is not this join's to classify, but it is worth a later act's attention when v9 is applied.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX, with no advisories. Sixteen attacks run, none landed. Read the disclosure first: I rejected v1 on one finding and Codex found two more I had missed. One was a key that contradicted its own value — v1 keyed the member leftoverDesignOpenIsAFinding while the value said the opposite; I checked the value, found it correct, praised it, and never read the key. The other was the fourteen FX fixture classes: I enumerated D-042's and D-093's unmet lists, which is how I found the actor-join gap, and stopped there instead of enumerating the pinned truth tables' own fixture-class container. That makes three pinned inventories I have failed to enumerate across these joins and one I caught; the corrective is coverage, not judgement. All three repairs land and I verified each against primary bytes. The FX set I derived independently from v9's acceptanceEvidenceFixtureClasses before reading the obligation, and it is set-equal to the fourteen listed; the leftover classification is right on v9's own discipline field, which says these are specifications of exact-byte intent and no fixture exists. The renamed member drops the old key entirely and keeps the value byte-identical, still correct against DR-105's live OPEN cell. The actor-join obligation routes the limb to DR-114 on D-093's own labelling, with D-129's candidate correctly described as binding nothing, and the staleness field now answers both limbs where it previously answered one. The change is strictly additive: two obligations added, none removed, leftover grown by the FX item only, a sixteen-way partition with no overlap, and every earlier group, refusal and reason preserved. I also tested whether the join's refusal to enumerate v9's fourteen identityDependencies is principled, since at the DR-104 join I advised carrying an omitted ride. It is: there the join had carried four of five and the fifth's absence was inconsistent, whereas here it enumerates none and states why, and the one ID-DEP that overlaps the adopted unmet list is carried as OBL-G09-EXECUTION. Worth a later act's attention when v9 is applied: v9 records ID-DEP-P13 as the one ride in its list with no owner named.
